headline: High-risk git/workspace interaction: Aider can write and commit shared repo state while LightZero is non-writing, making prompt injection and cascading errors the main concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and can execute shell commands, so attacker-controlled repo content could influence its instructions. LightZero has no file or network I/O, so it is not an active injector, but the shared repo path creates a plausible bridge. The pathway exists in default coding workflows, though not via MCP or clipboard.
conditions: IF LightZero or another process writes attacker-controlled text into the shared git repo, Aider may ingest it as instructions.
IF Aider is configured to act on repository content without provenance checks, prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Restrict Aider to a dedicated branch or repo copy.
Add a manual review step for any repo text that could be interpreted as instructions.
Disable automatic execution of repo-sourced commands or prompts.
Use file allowlists for Aider edits.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for repo content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider can read the filesystem and handles source code and git history, while LightZero has no filesystem read, write, or network egress. There is no evidence LightZero can exfiltrate data, so leakage between them is limited to the shared repo and is small unless sensitive files are placed there. The pair does not show a default third-party leak path from B.
conditions: IF sensitive files are stored in the shared git workspace, Aider can read them.
IF LightZero is extended with file access or logging of repo contents, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared repo.
Use a separate workspace for Aider.
Rotate any credentials accidentally committed.
Limit Aider to non-sensitive paths.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has write access and modifies git state; LightZero has no write, shell, or subprocess capability, so direct write-write conflict is absent. The only overlap is the shared git repo, but B cannot mutate it. This makes capability conflict unlikely and bounded to Aider-only changes.
conditions: IF LightZero is wrapped with external tooling that adds write access, git conflicts become possible.
IF multiple Aider instances edit the same repo without locking, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Use one writer per branch.
Enable git locking or a merge queue.
Run LightZero read-only.
Review Aider commits before merge.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate and commit code changes, and LightZero is a game-playing system with no documented verification role. If LightZero consumes Aider-produced artifacts as authoritative inputs, errors can cascade into incorrect downstream behavior. The pair lacks evidence of a built-in verification step, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF LightZero is fed Aider-generated files or configs as authoritative inputs, cascading errors are possible.
IF Aider commits incorrect code or data and LightZero uses it without validation, downstream behavior can be wrong.
mitigations: Add a validation step before LightZero consumes Aider outputs.
Require human review of Aider commits.
Use tests or schema checks on generated artifacts.
Separate generation and execution environments.
requires-engineering: implement typed handoff contracts.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and may handle API keys via env vars, while LightZero touches no data classes and has no stated compliance surface. The main compliance issue is accidental inclusion of secrets or regulated code in Aider-managed repos; LightZero does not add a separate residency or certification mismatch. One-agent citation is sufficient because the risk is Aider-side only.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are committed into the shared repo, Aider may process them.
IF the repo is subject to retention or deletion obligations, git history may complicate compliance.
mitigations: Exclude secrets from git history.
Use .gitignore and secret scanning.
Purge accidental commits quickly.
Keep regulated data out of the workspace.
requires-engineering: add retention-aware repo controls.
